articles.title: GTA 5's Michael Actor Defends GTA 6 After Doubters Say Rockstar's Games Look Too Similar
articles.summary: Ned Luke, the actor behind Grand Theft Auto 5 's Michael De Santa, said people who think Grand Theft Auto 6 looks too much like GTA 5 are "out of their minds." Luke has remained an important figure in the GTA community since he first appeared as one of three playable professional criminals in the…
body: One of the many, many talking points to emerge in the wake of last week's GTA 6: Extended Look was that playing as protagonists Jason and Lucia looked a little too similar to the kind of gameplay one could expect from GTA 5. While most seem to believe Rockstar has wisely used the 13 years since that game's release, it hasn't stopped skepticism from creeping in.

Luke doesn't seem to be included in the new game's cast, but he still made sure to refute some of the criticisms popping up online while collaborating with YouTube channels Partychat and House of Highlights. When asked for his thoughts about those who believe there are too many similarities between GTA 5 and GTA 6, he made his stance clear.
"This looks nothing like Grand Theft Auto 5," he said. "I think they're out of their minds."
"I'll tell you one thing: I never looked that good," he added, pointing to an image of Jason on his screen."

articles.title: Yellowstone and Lioness Games Could Be in Paramount Games' Future
articles.summary: Paramount, the multimedia giant behind huge IP like Avatar: The Last Airbender, SpongeBob SquarePants, and Star Trek, has felt the wind shift. The company announced during Summer Game Fest that it would be venturing headfirst into the vast world of video games with its new games division, Paramount…
body: Alongside the announcement of the studio's debut, Paramount Game Studios also revealed its collaboration with action-game developer PlatinumGames, the studio behind Bayonetta. The developer will be working on an adaptation of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin, whose trailer revealed little beyond a sneak peek at a grim-looking, futuristic New York.

However, The Last Ronin is just the first step for Paramount Games Studio's projects. In June, Polygon spoke with Shawn Kittelsen, head of creative and production at Paramount Games Studio, who revealed more about what to expect from the studio.

While Kittelsen revealed that the "core four" properties Paramount Games is targeting are Ninja Turtles, Star Trek, Avatar: The Last Airbender, and SpongeBob SquarePants, the executive confirmed the "Sheridanverse" — referring to Yellowstone's creator, Taylor Sheridan — is also a property Paramount Games is interested in building upon.
"All of the Yellowstone and Yellowstone-adjacent titles, Landman, Tulsa King, these are all priorities for us," Kittelsen tells Polygon.

articles.title: The 90-Minute Action Thriller Quentin Tarantino Called "My Favorite" Is Officially Free on Streaming
articles.summary: There’s always been a deep irony that follows holiday horror films. Typically, we associate holidays like Christmas and Valentine’s Day with whimsical joy, togetherness, and romance. Slapping the horror genre on saccharine happiness feels like kicking someone while their back is turned mid-hug.
body: On the other end of the spectrum, haters of the holidays will feel right at home with holiday horror. If that’s the case for you, then you owe it to yourself to give My Bloody Valentine a try now that it's free to stream on Pluto TV.

Directed by George Mihalka with a screenplay by John Beaird, My Bloody Valentine takes place in the small mining town of Valentine Bluffs. Two decades before the movie begins, two supervisors working at the mine leave early to attend a Valentine’s Day party in town, while, unbeknownst to them, a cave collapse strands the remaining group of men. A year after the collapse, the only survivor gets his revenge. He murders those two supervisors and leaves their hearts in a box of Valentine’s Day chocolate with a warning for the town: If they ever host a Valentine’s Day dance again, he’ll return to killing.

articles.title: Star Wars and Jurassic Park VFX Legend Phil Tippett Closes Studio and Auctions Memorabilia
articles.summary: Phil Tippett – the Oscar-winning animator and visual effects supervisor whose dazzling stop-motion animation work appears in the original Star Wars trilogy, 1987’s RoboCop, and Jurassic Park – has announced the closure of his Berkeley, California studio.
body: Tippett, 74, sold his work – including memorabilia and props – at a two-day auction held this weekend, the artist informed the Berkeleyside news site (via FilmStories ).

The items auctioned at the liquidation sale – the result of Tippett Studio’s Chapter 11 bankruptcy – included stop-motion models of AT-ATs from Empire Strikes Back, autographed posters from Jurassic World and The Mandalorian, and much more ( click here to view the full gallery of Tippett’s collection).
The pioneering animator was inspired to pursue a career in stop-motion animation after seeing Ray Harryhausen's The 7th Voyage of Sinbad as a child.

During his four-decade-long film career, Tippett worked for Industrial Light & Magic on the Dejarik game scene in Star Wars: A New Hope, 1981’s Dragonslayer, and 1983’s Return of the Jedi, which won Tippett his first Academy Award for visual effects. He also won for Jurassic Park.

articles.title: Fable's Main Quest Will Take About 20 Hours to Beat
articles.summary: Fable 's main quest will take around 20 hours to beat, Playground Games has confirmed. Associate game directors Will Kennedy and Craig Littler shared the estimated length for the 2027 fantasy RPG during a group Q&A attended by Polygon at gamescom 2026.
body: "We have around 15-20 hours of mainline quest gameplay, we have around 15-20 of side and open-world exploration content gameplay," Kennedy said.

As sprawling RPGs have continued to fill the space, that might come up a bit short for what some players were expecting. Open-world games like Elden Ring, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, and Assassin's Creed Valhalla have famously delivered massive worlds with main quests that could have players spending 50 hours or more just to complete the story. For Fable, that won't be the case, but longtime fans probably expected that.

Howlongtobeat has the original 2004 Fable 's main quest clocking in at about 12 and a half hours. Fable 2 isn't much longer at 13 hours, and Fable 3 inches just further past that at 13 and a half hours. If anything, next year's Fable reboot is already shaping up to be the longest in the series, and pushing its main campaign on much longer would have it launching with a story almost twice as long as the one in the original game.

articles.title: A Incredible Looking and Unofficial 'Zelda Maker 64' Is Coming to Steam
articles.summary: After Super Mario Maker, you'd think Nintendo would give its other retro franchises a similar DIY treatment. Since the Japanese company hasn't, other game developers are filling the void instead.
body: Temple Maker 64 is the work of Akela-morse, a solo game developer who left his job a year and a half ago to focus on the idea full-time. In an exchange with Polygon, the 27-year-old creative says that he got the idea after seeing titles like Quest Master, Super Dungeon Maker, and Super Dungeon Designer. But since all of these titles are top-down 2D pixel art games, "going with a N64 aesthetic felt evident," he said.

The level design suite gives players all the classic weapons, items, and enemies they'd expect from a 3D Zelda game like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — but Temple Maker 64 is careful not to use any names Nintendo uses. Similarly, the tunic-clad protagonist is highly reminiscent of Link without necessarily copying his design. Threading the needle like this might help Temple Maker 64 find an established audience. High-profile attempts to sell similar ideas, like Amazon's dungeon-making party game King of Meat, have floundered even as they've offered extensive level design and community-focused sharing features.

articles.title: The Definitive ’90s Sci-Fi Action Blockbuster Is Officially Streaming for Free on YouTube
articles.summary: There’s something so refreshing about the simplicity of a great '90s adventure movie. Some of my personal favorites are the ones that don’t take themselves too seriously.
body: Enter Roland Emmerich's Stargate. The 1994 action-adventure movie with a sci-fi twist drops Egyptologist Daniel Jackson (James Spader) and Special Forces Colonel Jack O'Neil (Kurt Russell) into an otherworldly Egypt after unlocking a portal that allows access across the universe. The basic setup makes the story feel like a lost-civilization adventure before it becomes a traditional alien-invasion story. There are ancient gods, mysterious hieroglyphics, buried secrets, enormous temples, and an entire civilization living under the thumb of a supposed god.

Emmerich’s execution of Stargate stands out precisely because it predates the destructive spectacle that later defined his career. Coming just two years after Universal Soldier, Stargate catches Emmerich in a more patient directing style. Instead of relying on the apocalyptic set pieces of Independence Day or The Day After Tomorrow, his direction prioritizes world-building, atmospheric tension, and the quiet awe of sci-fi exploration. The result is a sharper film that lets a high-concept premise breathe more naturally, like the gradual unfolding of the mystery of the Stargate before its characters even enter the desert landscape.
points: There’s something so refreshing about the simplicity of a great '90s adventure movie.
Some of my personal favorites are the ones that don’t take themselves too seriously.

articles.title: GTA 6 Fans Think They Found Jason and Lucia's Vice City Apartment in Real Life
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans think they've spotted the real-life inspiration for Jason and Lucia's Vice City apartment – but don't expect to ever visit it yourself. Grand Theft Auto players have proven time and time again that they will go to the ends of the earth to learn the smallest details about…
body: Instagram user prettyboycuh was the first to publicly share the location, saying they started by using Google Maps to find a tall teal building that was first shown in last week's gameplay trailer. They said "that was easy," but when they used the Street View function to turn to where Jason and Lucia's apartment should be, all they found was a patch of grass. Then, they turned back the clock.

They – and you can still see this for yourself, too – changed the map's time period from March 2026 to April 2013, around four months before the launch of GTA 5, and voila, the apartment appeared. Rockstar hasn't officially confirmed what was known as the Belmar Condominium to be the inspiration for the spot we see Jason and Lucia hanging out at in GTA 6, but the similarities are too difficult to ignore. It's the same color, has the same fence, many of the buildings around it are the same, and we can even see the parking lot Jason pulled out of in the extended look. So, where'd it go?

articles.title: Activision sends a legal rep to a Call of Duty cheat seller's front door, films the whole thing, posts it online
articles.summary: Activision has posted footage of one of its legal representatives turning up at the Ohio home of a notorious Call of Duty cheat seller and handing over a cease-and-desist order.
body: The roughly one-minute clip went up on the official Call of Duty account on Friday, although the cease and desist was actually served on 22nd August, during last weekend's Modern Warfare 4 closed beta.
It shows a representative pulling up outside a house, meeting a man whose face is blurred throughout, and handing over paperwork.
"I just got some paperwork for you," he said. "Attorneys for Activision and, uh, it's a cease-and-desist order for you."
He tells the man to contact the attorney's office listed on the documents and leaves. No shouting, no chase, no drama – just papers served on a doorstep.

articles.title: A Star Wars Galaxies community server was allegedly hacked with AI assistance by a Reddit moderator harboring a primeval grudge
articles.summary: Star Wars Galaxies Legends, one of many community servers offering a version of the defunct MMO with custom additions, reportedly had its assets decrypted by a hacker with the username levarrishawk (via Massively OP ).
body: "[W]e’ve confirmed that Levarris, aka levarrishawk from r/swg, used AI tools to decrypt our client side game asset files," the Discord post reads. "This gave him access to assets from all of our custom content: items, questlines … We do know that he’s actively offered these files to other servers, and while we can’t confirm that he’s had any takers yet, if you start seeing Legends‑exclusive content out in other worlds it was likely taken from us.
"We’re obviously bothered by this, but there isn’t much we can do outside of being upfront with all of you and staying focused on what makes Legends great."

Notably, no player data or personal info was accessed. The response from Levarris, who is a moderator for the Star Wars Galaxies subreddit, reveals the motivation behind this hack: some drama that goes back "roughly fourteen years ago."

articles.title: Total War: Warhammer 40,000 wins best PC game at Gamescom
articles.summary: When Total War: Warhammer first debuted, I was much more into the wargame setting's sci-fi counterpart. This would be cool if Space Marines were in it, I remember thinking, somehow unaware that Total War: Warhammer would end up being one of the best strategy games on PC.
body: It's the third award Sega took home this year, along with best audio for Alien: Isolation 2 and best lineup for its whole gaggle of games. It's easy to see why, particularly in the case of Total War 40K—PC Gamer's Fraser Brown said it took a mere hour of playtime to cement the game as the highlight of his year. "It's immediately obvious how special Total War 40k is—I don't think a tutorial has ever made me giddy before," he wrote.

According to Gamescom's website, the winners are chosen "by both an expert jury of gaming professionals and the community." In other words, it was a favorite among both professional nerds and the pro bono sort.

If it wasn’t clear before why people have been so vocally insistent that this game should happen ever since Total War first embraced fantasy, it should be now: there are many ways to adapt Warhammer 40,000's galaxy-spanning eternal war in videogame form, but Total War's combination of scale and gruesome, exacting detail seems a particularly good fit.

articles.title: Phasmophobia's second Quality of Life update adds Restricted maps, VR fixes, and much creepier deaths
articles.summary: Kinetic Games has released Phasmophobia 's second Quality of Life update, adding a raft of new Restricted maps, streamlined Evidence collection, VR fixes, and considerably more ways to die.
body: Now live on PC and PlayStation (the Xbox release is "to follow"), the Quality of Life Part 2 update builds on Quality of Life Part 1 which introduced the revamped 13 Willow Street map back in July alongside a batch of other gameplay tweaks.

We're getting a (long-overdue!) set of new small-to-medium Restricted maps for Prison, Brownstone High School, and Point Hope, bringing condensed versions of the original maps designed to speed up investigations and add more variety to runs.

Evidence collection has also been streamlined. Rather than manually checking the in-game journal, players can now tell whether a piece of evidence has already been logged directly from their Photo Camera, Video Camera, or Sound Recorder via faded overlays and yellow LEDs.
Evidence and ghost types selected by teammates will also now show up for the whole team, cutting down on last-minute double-checking before a hunt.

articles.title: Thanks to a dedicated team 'art-directing' every single NPC, GTA 6 has over 10 times as many unique animations as GTA 5
articles.summary: There are big-budget blockbusters, and then there's GTA 6. If you want any sense of just how big this thing is, look no further than a recent interview Rockstar North co-head Aaron Garbut gave The New York Times (via Techradar ).
body: "We art-directed each individual one of them," Garbut said in the interview. "Every room in the game, somebody thought about this … Who's sitting where, what they're drinking, the marks that are left on the table. The pictures on the wall will have the people that are in that room, with their tattoos on their arms and their family behind them.

"That whole thing has been made, and built, and photographed, and placed in this random room in a random building in a huge city, in a world." He revealed that GTA 6 has over 600,000 animations—double the amount Red Dead Redemption 2 had, both of which dwarf GTA 5's 55,000. Considering the game's map is also three times as big as Red Dead 2's, it seems like the game operates on an unprecedented level of scale and fidelity.

This all lines up with what PC Gamer's US editor-in-chief Tyler Wilde said of the game in the wake of recent leaks earlier this month: even if GTA 6 doesn't reinvent the open world crime-'em-up, it "will be impressive for the same reason Rockstar games typically are: The absurd amount of effort and money the studio puts into making them as big and detailed as the mainstream hardware of the day can manage."

articles.title: 12TB Valve archive leak includes early Portal 2 builds and hints of Half-Life 2: Episode Three
articles.summary: A leaked archive said to contain around 12TB of old Valve development files, dated between 2003 and 2013, has surfaced online, and fans are already combing through it for any trace of the long-cancelled Half-Life 2: Episode Three.
body: The leak was first flagged on Friday by Twitter/X user Gabe Follower, who said the archive included early versions of Portal 2, Left 4 Dead, and CS:GO, along with assets from the cancelled Portal prequel F-Stop, and "potentially" material tied to Episode Three.

So far, the leak is thought to contain a 2009-era Portal 2 beta build alongside a model for the "Weaponizer", a weapon previously associated (if never confirmed) with Episode Three, though here apparently repurposed as a placeholder asset within Portal 2 itself.

Elsewhere in the archive, people have identified a fully playable Left 4 Dead beta build dated June 2008, complete with an early HUD, a work-in-progress lobby screen, and cut audio, including lines originally recorded for Zoey by Alésia Glidewell before Jen Taylor replaced her in the final game.
The material reportedly comes from Valve's old Steam2 content-delivery infrastructure, which the studio phased out in favour of SteamPipe in the early 2010s.
